digest:
Context Pack: heat pumps (Wärmepumpen) for home heating, purchase decisions, costs, subsidies and experiences (DE, Homeowners in Germany (owner-occupied houses, typically 35-70) considering, planning or already operating a heat pump, often replacing a gas or oil heating). Coverage grade c; 212 relevant posts. Thin evidence.
Five truths: [OBJ-02] Get a heat load calculation done first before you decide. [THM-03] I can't tell if an offer is fair when the items are not broken out. [THM-08] Installer prices will not come down when the subsidy shrinks. [MOM-05] I weigh when to heat between a low tariff and a worse COP at night. [OBJ-04] Heat pumps in Germany are far too expensive because of the subsidy.

Heizlastberechnung, Zählerschrank, Altbestand-Entsorgung), and ask members which positions their own quote was missing. snapshot.represents: 212 public posts from about 194 people, mostly on Facebook and X. This is what vocal people say online, not a survey of the whole market.

position.statement: Know what you're paying for: itemised quotes, real-world numbers
position.for_whom: Hausbesitzer mit Altbau (oder alter Gas-/Ölheizung), die ein Angebot für eine WP in der Hand haben und nicht einschätzen können, ob Preis und Komponenten passen
position.against_doubt: "Ich kann nicht beurteilen, ob das Angebot fair ist und ob die WP bei mir im Winter wirklich effizient läuft, oder ob sie sich je rechnet."

top_opportunity.text: Comprehensive rental economics case showing landlord ROI, profitability thresholds, and investment payback scenarios.

top_risk.text: Heat pumps and the Heizungsgesetz are politically charged: posts frame them as a culture war or as a government scandal. Brand messaging that takes a side may trigger backlash.

snapshot.grade_note: Capped at c: the sources are broad (grade b), but too few findings met the minimum bar.

generic_points: Homeowners are mainly worried about high upfront costs and want clarity on total investment versus long-term savings on energy bills.
Government subsidies (BEG/KfW grants) are a major motivator, but the application process and changing rules create confusion and frustration.
Many fear that a heat pump won't work efficiently in older, poorly insulated houses and worry about needing expensive renovations first.
Rising gas and oil prices and CO2 taxes push owners to look for independence from fossil fuels and more future-proof heating.
Uncertainty about the Gebäudeenergiegesetz (Heizungsgesetz) and political debates make people hesitant and desire legal certainty.
Trust in installers is a key issue, with long waiting times, skilled labor shortages, and difficulty comparing quotes.
Homeowners worry about electricity costs, running costs, and the efficiency (COP/JAZ) of the system, and consider combining with photovoltaics and storage.
Noise from outdoor units, neighbor relations and placement/space requirements are common practical concerns.
People search online via Google, YouTube, forums, comparison portals and consumer advice centers, and value independent, neutral information and peer experiences.
Effective messaging stresses savings, subsidies, comfort, climate protection and reliability, backed by real-world case studies and transparent cost calculators.
Existing users share experiences about efficiency, hydraulic balancing, and optimization, and are generally satisfied but sometimes disappointed by higher-than-expected bills.
Trends include growing heat pump sales, falling prices, more heat pump electricity tariffs, and increasing interest in smart control and hybrid solutions.

for_goals.headline: German heat pump owners and prospects are mainly asking one thing: is this price fair and will it pay off in my house? They trust peers' itemised quotes and measured winter values more than brochure claims (HYP-03 is supported, the rest is observation).
for_goals.success_measure: Replies in the first 2-4 weeks that add missing quote positions, share JAZ/Vorlauftemperatur values or repeat the same radiator or flow-temperature question, showing which topics to build content on.

do_first.action: Post a checklist carousel in public German heat pump groups on Facebook: "Diese Positionen muss ein WP-Angebot enthalten" (incl. Heizlastberechnung, Zählerschrank, Altbestand-Entsorgung), and ask members which positions their own quote was missing.
do_first.why: Quote comparison is the most non-obvious, repeated need: owners can't judge offers when items aren't broken out, and they already post quotes and ask groups.

creative_brief.objective: Understand the audience and build trust by helping owners judge offers and efficiency themselves, using their own numbers and wording.
creative_brief.audience: Hausbesitzer in Deutschland (ca. 35-70), Altbau oder alte Gas-/Ölheizung, mit Angebot oder frisch installierter WP; viele rechnen selbst und vertrauen anderen Besitzern mehr als Herstellern.
creative_brief.insight: They want savings but can't tell from a single total whether the price is fair or the pump will deliver in their house in winter, so they ask peers to check.
creative_brief.message: Mit Einzelpositionen und realen Werten kannst du Angebot und WP selbst beurteilen.
creative_brief.tone: Blunt, practical, number-first, informal German; matter-of-fact, no hype or sales language; admit limits and frame unverified items as observations.
mandatories: reale Werte / JAZ incl. winter values
Amortisation shown as a calculation, not a promise
avoid: Advertising a best-case SCOP without winter values
Promising that prices fall when subsidies shrink
Presenting a big national provider as the trusted choice

objection_handling.response: Verständlich, aber ein Gesamtpreis sagt nichts. Lass dir das Angebot mit Einzelpositionen geben (Gerät, Speicher, Zählerschrank, Entsorgung, Montage) und hol Vergleichsangebote ein, dann siehst du, wo der Preis herkommt. Adapt to your offer: show your own itemised structure and what is included in each position.

Stimmt: erst die Heizlastberechnung, dann entscheiden. Sie zeigt, welche Leistung dein Haus wirklich braucht, und ohne sie ist jedes Angebot geraten. Adapt to your offer: state whether a heat load calculation is included, who does it, and when you deliver it.

Wer über 15 Jahre skeptisch ist, hat recht, das zu hinterfragen. Rechne Öl- oder Gaskosten gegen WP-Strom Zeile für Zeile und nimm reale Werte statt Prospektwerte. Die Amortisation hängt von deinem Haus, deinem Strompreis und der Förderung ab. Adapt to your offer: give a transparent calculation template with your own prices and conditions, no promised payback.

Viele sagen das und sehen die Preise kritisch. Wir versprechen nicht, dass Preise sinken, wenn die Förderung schrumpft. Vergleich Angebote mit Einzelpositionen und prüf, was davon wirklich nötig ist. Adapt to your offer: show which positions you charge for and how the subsidy enters your calculation.

Viele setzen auf den örtlichen Installateur und entscheiden nach Vertrauen. Frag nach Referenzen, lass dir Einzelpositionen geben und hol Vergleichsangebote ein; Erfahrungen anderer Besitzer helfen mehr als Werbung. Adapt to your offer: if you work locally, say so with regional references, otherwise point to how owners can vet any installer.

Berechtigte Frage. Der Aufstellort und der Abstand zum Nachbarn gehören vor dem Kauf geklärt. Frag nach den Schallwerten der Geräte und nach alternativen Standorten im Angebot. Adapt to your offer: state the sound data of your devices and what placement advice you give.

Nicht pauschal. Entscheidend ist, welche Vorlauftemperatur dein Haus bei der Heizlast wirklich braucht. Miss sie, schau dir die Heizkennlinie an und frag Besitzer mit ähnlichem Altbau nach ihren JAZ-Werten. Adapt to your offer: say how you check the flow temperature needed and which Altbau cases you can show.

Dazu gibt es unterschiedliche Erfahrungen: Manche berichten, dass es im Altbau läuft, andere sehen Probleme. Entscheidend sind Heizlast, Heizkörper und Vorlauftemperatur deines Hauses, nicht eine Faustregel. Adapt to your offer: say for which house types your products fit and which checks you do first.

Eine einzelne Stimme, die wir als Beobachtung nehmen und nicht als Fakt. Frag nach Herstellerangaben, Garantie, Wartung und Ersatzteilen, und lass dir das ins Angebot schreiben. Adapt to your offer: state your warranty, service and spare-parts terms.

hypotheses.statement: Running costs and electricity prices, plus uncertainty about the actual efficiency (JAZ) in an older house, worry German homeowners more than the purchase price itself.
hypotheses.why: Posts raise running costs and savings, and doubt headline efficiency values (SCOP in winter, a JAZ of 2.6). But purchase price and payback are raised just as sharply, so the evidence does not show running costs worry owners more than price.

hypotheses.statement: Distrust of political changes (Gebäudeenergiegesetz/"Heizungsgesetz", BEG funding) delays decisions and makes homeowners wait or choose a new gas boiler.
hypotheses.why: Political posts show strong emotions about the Heizungsgesetz, and one landlord hopes the old boiler lasts until there are 'smarter politicians', while an installer notes people waiting for lower prices. No post shows a switch to a new gas boiler.

hypotheses.statement: Homeowners trust peer experience reports from other owners and independent energy consultants more than manufacturer or installer claims.
hypotheses.why: Owners ask peers for opinions on offers, cite measured data and databases, and warn against marketing figures or national providers. Independent energy consultants are barely visible, and one is criticised for fees, so only the peer part is clearly shown.

hypotheses.statement: Installer availability, quality of heat-load calculation and long waiting times are top frustrations, and a bad installation experience shapes perception of the technology.
hypotheses.why: Heat load calculation, trust in installers and scarcity of installers show up, and one Dutch post says no installer can be found. The evidence does not show these as top frustrations or how a bad installation shapes views.

hypotheses.statement: Owners of older, unrenovated houses doubt that a heat pump works without full insulation or underfloor heating, and this is the main objection.

risks.text: Heat pumps and the Heizungsgesetz are politically charged: posts frame them as a culture war or as a government scandal. Brand messaging that takes a side may trigger backlash.
Naming or comparing national providers like Enpal or 1komma5 can feed existing distrust. Claims that sound too good (halved electricity cost, all-in prices) are already met with suspicion.
Efficiency claims such as SCOP or JAZ figures are doubted by owners, who point to winter values and measured data. Quoting brochure numbers risks being mocked.
Subsidy answers must be right: owners ask about eligibility and proofs, and a wrong or outdated answer could harm trust, as the rules are said to be changing.
Price talk is sensitive: offers are called absurd and subsidies are blamed for high prices, so a brand pointing to subsidies or high quotes may look like part of the problem.
Several posts are Dutch-language and from the Dutch market and single posts back some themes (lifespan, noise, comfort), so applying them to German homeowners may be a misreading.
